title: What If You Sneezed With Your Eyes Open?

scenes.text: What if you sneezed with your eyes open? The famous warning is wrong.
Almost everyone's eyes slam shut when they sneeze. It's a reflex, and it's hard to override.
But it can be done. Doctors say it's possible, just difficult.
And your eyes would stay put. Nothing in your nose or throat connects to the space behind your eyeballs.
So why close them at all? One idea: it keeps whatever you sneeze out from blowing back into your eyes.
Scientists still aren't sure. You've sneezed thousands of times, and nobody can tell you exactly why your eyes shut.

description:
What if you sneezed with your eyes open? It's possible with effort, and doctors say a sneeze is extremely unlikely to make an eyeball pop out: the airways aren't connected to the space behind the eye.
Why we close our eyes is still debated; one theory is protection from the irritants we expel.
